Here's a description of the provided plot, following the guidelines:

The plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics. The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence”, is a linear scale ranging from 0.71 to 1.00 with tick labels at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy”, is a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. A blue line with circular markers and error bars represents “Final Accuracy”, starting at approximately 0.66 at an initial confidence of 0.71 and ending at approximately 0.91 at an initial confidence of 1.00, with fluctuations between these points, including a minimum of 0.84 at an initial confidence of 0.87. An orange line with diamond markers and error bars represents “Δ Accuracy”, beginning at approximately 0.24 at an initial confidence of 0.71 and decreasing to approximately 0.06 at an initial confidence of 1.00, with a minimum of approximately -0.04 at an initial confidence of 0.94. A green line with square markers and error bars represents “Initial Accuracy”, starting at approximately 0.74 at an initial confidence of 0.71 and increasing to approximately 0.88 at an initial confidence of 1.00, with a minimum of approximately 0.66 at an initial confidence of 0.83.
